entries.product: Microsoft Copilot Chat (formerly Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat)
entries.feature: Web-grounded AI chat for work accounts: drafting and rewriting, analysis of uploaded files, image generation. Organisational content is used only when the user pastes or uploads it. Standard access, subject to service capacity.
entries.processingLocation: Microsoft says Copilot Chat calls to the model go to the closest datacentres in the region but can go to other regions when demand is high, and customers outside the EU 'may have their queries processed in the US, EU, or other regions'. Web search queries go to Bing, outside the Microsoft 365 service boundary. Prompts and responses are stored in Exchange in the tenant, for audit and eDiscovery.

entries.feature: Chat in Outlook that answers from the user's own emails, calendar, meetings, chats and a bounded set of OneDrive and SharePoint files, without a Copilot add-on licence. Client, mailbox and configuration requirements apply.
entries.processingLocation: Microsoft says model calls go to the closest datacentres in the region but can go to other regions when demand is high, and customers outside the EU 'may have their queries processed in the US, EU, or other regions'.

entries.product: Microsoft Copilot Business (add-on licence; formerly Microsoft 365 Copilot)
entries.feature: Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams that reasons across the user's emails, meetings, chats, documents and sites (Graph, Work IQ and semantic indexing), with priority access and advanced agent experiences.
entries.processingLocation: Microsoft says model calls go to the closest datacentres in the region but can go to other regions when demand is high, and customers outside the EU 'may have their queries processed in the US, EU, or other regions'. Microsoft says in-country inferencing for Microsoft 365 Copilot is 'expected' in Australia by the end of 2026. Prompts, responses and citations are stored under the tenant's Microsoft 365 data residency commitments; Anthropic and OpenAI models are offered as subprocessors that an admin can choose to enable.

entries.feature: Conversational assistant inside Xero: answers questions about the business's own financials with charts and tables, general business research, and help with admin tasks such as creating invoices or quotes. Users see only data their Xero permissions allow.
entries.processingLocation: Not published for AI processing. Xero says JAX uses third-party model providers (AWS, Microsoft Azure, GCP, OpenAI) that don't retain the data or train on it. Xero's subprocessor list gives each provider's entity country (United States), not where inference runs. Xero's privacy notice says data may be processed in Australia, New Zealand and the United States.

entries.product: Zoom Workplace (ZoomMate features included in the plan)

entries.processingLocation: Zoom says accounts hosted in its AU region use Zoom's own models plus third-party models on dedicated Amazon Bedrock instances (not sent to the model providers), or Zoom-hosted models only if the customer chooses. Accounts hosted in the US default to a federated approach that can send data to third-party providers such as Anthropic and OpenAI, under zero-retention terms.
